teaser.en: Drive the south coast road in season and you will see piles of green-skinned oranges for sale at the roadside.

summary.en: *Mchungwa* is the sweet orange, an evergreen citrus tree grown on farms and around homesteads. South coast oranges are sold at roadsides and eaten fresh or as juice.

about.en:
*Mchungwa* is an evergreen tree with a rounded crown, glossy dark green leaves and sometimes small thorns. Its white flowers are strongly scented.

The fruits, *chungbwa*, are round, with a thick, fragrant skin. In the warm coastal climate, the skin often stays green or greenish-yellow even when the fruit inside is ripe and sweet.

where.en: Orange trees grow on farms and around homesteads along the south coast. In season, the fruit is sold at roadside stalls.

uses.en: Oranges are eaten fresh and squeezed for juice. They are also sold for cash, often at roadsides.

names.en: Digo: *mchungwa* for the tree and *chungbwa* for the fruit. Swahili: *mchungwa*, with the fruit called *chungwa*. English: sweet orange. Scientists call it *Citrus sinensis*.

reason.en: Mango, another fruit sold at roadsides

definition.en: An orange (the fruit). Pakia spells it chungwa, with the tree mchungwa.

taxon.note: GBIF backbone lists C. sinensis as a synonym of C. aurantium (sour orange); POWO accepts Citrus × sinensis for sweet orange. Hand fix 2026-10-10.
